assessments.reasoning: I reacquired the identical archive PDF. Its title identifies the Ministry of Defence definition, the imprint reports a 1970 first publication and 1973 second impression, and the preface dated February 1973 identifies revisions. On PDF page 44, printed 34, Table I pairs the word-location formal with a word reference actual, and section 8.3.2 binds data-reference formals to the same locations as their actuals on entry. On PDF page 45, printed 35, section 8.3.2.1 makes index evaluation part of obtaining the location on entry, expressly requires an exact numeric type match, and excludes part-word references. This supports the stated time and referent for a permitted indexed word actual. The neighboring value, array and table rules preserve the claim boundaries.

challenge.method: Read the imprint, February 1973 preface, and printed pages 33 through 35 in the fresh scan. Challenged with a hypothetical caller array element whose index variable changes after callee entry, a numerically mismatched actual, a part-word field, and a formal changed to VALUE, ARRAY, or TABLE. Compared Table I and sections 8.3 through 8.3.2.3.
challenge.results: Section 8.3.2.1 resolves the word actual index on entry and section 8.3.2 keeps the formal at that location, so the hypothetical later index-variable change does not select another element. A numeric-type mismatch or part-word field fails the rule. VALUE evaluates and assigns a numerical value to its formal. An ARRAY formal admits the array name and body indexing can select its elements. TABLE has a distinct formal specification excluding presetting. None is a counterexample to the exact word LOCATION claim.

limitations: The rule applies to valid indexed word references supplied to a word LOCATION formal in the impression identified by the February 1973 preface. Compiler behavior and other impressions fall outside the claim.
A whole-word table element can be a word-reference actual. A part-word element is excluded. Separate ARRAY and TABLE formal categories have their own rules.
